claim_statement: Fixed takeover time budgets (e.g., 4s, 7s) fail to guarantee physical recoverability across varied kinematics and vehicle dynamics.
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Fixed scalar time budgets do not account for kinematic state variations and vehicle deceleration physics, as previously highlighted by Papadimitriou et al. (2024) and Deng et al. (2024).
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming that our work is the first to identify that fixed TOR budgets are insufficient or the first to argue for including braking time in takeover evaluation.

claim_statement: Human driver reaction latency t1 exhibits substantial variability under non-driving secondary tasks (bounded in [0.7, 1.5] s).
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Driver reaction latency is modeled as an exogenous interval [0.7, 1.5] s grounded in recent empirical takeover benchmarks.
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming that we developed a new cognitive model of human perception and reaction.

claim_statement: Emergency takeover braking response before a critical stationary obstacle can be approximated by an open-loop full-brake step demand.
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Drivers in critical takeover emergencies frequently apply maximum emergency braking, supporting a full-brake step approximation.
prohibited_overclaim: Asserting that all real-world human drivers behave as pure open-loop step controllers in all contexts.

claim_statement: Pre-effective-human-braking longitudinal deceleration (a_pre) ranges between 0.0 and 3.0 m/s^2 depending on vehicle deceleration dynamics.
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Pre-effective deceleration during reaction latency is bounded within [0.0, 3.0] m/s^2 based on published EV regenerative and conventional deceleration data.
prohibited_overclaim: Asserting EV safety superiority or generalizing beyond the bounded longitudinal kinematic window.

claim_statement: Physical brake systems introduce deceleration-response delay t2 (0.05-0.17 s) and response build-up time t3 (0.15-0.45 s).
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Braking deceleration is mediated by a response delay and a linear ramp-up phase bounded by empirical braking literature.
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming novel discovery of brake system lag or actuator mechanics.

claim_statement: Automated takeover literature has predominantly focused on driver cognitive factors while neglecting vehicle deceleration transients.
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: While prior work has introduced maneuver execution time into takeover safety (e.g. Papadimitriou et al., 2024), existing models continue to treat vehicle deceleration as point-mass or empirical traces, omitting analytical transient decomposition.
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming no prior researcher ever thought about vehicle braking or authority-transition safety.

claim_statement: The minimum takeover lead time T_required before a stationary hazard is given by an exact closed-form algebraic expression.
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: We derive a closed-form algebraic expression for minimum required takeover lead time, extending classical point-mass models by explicitly decomposing pre-effective response and actuator transients.
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming priority on the general concept of stopping-based TOR triggering, or claiming an unprecedented mathematical discovery.

claim_statement: Pre-TOR acceleration history does not independently affect post-TOR recoverability once state (x_TOR, v_TOR) is fixed.
supporting_sources: Branch B0 Proof / L013 (Transp. Res. Part D 2025)
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Within a longitudinal Markov state formulation, pre-TOR acceleration history has no independent causal effect on stopping distance.
prohibited_overclaim: Generalizing history-independence to non-Markovian driver cognitive states or tire thermal dynamics.

claim_statement: Driver-vehicle internal model mismatch is non-identifiable on existing public datasets and has zero effect under full-brake step inputs.
supporting_sources: Branch C0 Audit / L012 (Transp. Res. Part F 2018), D001 (ADAS-TO 2024)
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Under the modeled full-brake step response, pedal gain mismatch has zero physical pathway to affect stopping distance; furthermore, naturalistic datasets lack vehicle familiarity labels.
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming driver unfamiliarity never matters in real-world driving.

claim_statement: The analytical oracle provides a strictly conservative upper bound on required time budget relative to numerical simulation.
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: The analytical boundary strictly upper-bounds numerical simulation across the parameter domain (T_oracle >= T_sim).
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming that the conservative bound proves absence of collision under unmodeled physical effects.

claim_statement: The proposed framework achieves parameter-level validation (V1) against published empirical datasets, while trajectory validation remains unidentifiable.
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Model parameters are grounded in empirical ranges (V1); direct trajectory and outcome validation remain bounded by public dataset limitations.
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming field-tested, vehicle-validated, or real-world crash-proven safety boundaries.

claim_statement: Pre-effective deceleration (a_pre) provides a substantial lead-time reduction across its bounded range, whereas response delay sets an irreducible offset.
supporting_sources: Branch A1 / D0 / E0 Results (NUM-08, NUM-10)
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Across its plausible span ([0, 3] m/s^2), pre-effective deceleration reduces required takeover lead time by ~0.44 s at nominal cruise speed (nominal marginal sensitivity ~ -0.155 s per m/s^2), which is roughly 3 to 4 times larger than the full span of brake response delay tuning (~0.12 s); response delay forms an irreducible offset.
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming an order-of-magnitude dominance over mechanical braking or recommending high deceleration without considering occupant comfort or rear-end risk.

claim_statement: When pre-effective deceleration and actuator transients are set to zero, the boundary algebraically reduces to the classical reaction-plus-constant-deceleration structure and the SUMO/TransAID MRM triggering threshold.
allowed_manuscript_phrasing: Setting a_pre = 0, t2 = 0, and t3 = 0 collapses the formulation to T_required = t1 + v0 / (2 a_max), reducing to the familiar reaction-distance plus constant-deceleration stopping-distance structure, corresponding to the simplified point-mass threshold used in SUMO/TransAID.
prohibited_overclaim: Claiming that our formulation is disconnected from classical traffic engineering foundations or claiming that SUMO proves universal industry standard practice.
